test_policy.notes: IUP's undergraduate admissions page says applicants do not need SAT or ACT scores to be accepted or to qualify for scholarships; the Common Data Set agrees: not required, considered if submitted. The international page asks for SAT/ACT only as an optional English-proficiency alternative for students who attended a US high school.

requirements.notes: International undergraduates apply on IUP's own online application ($25, payable online or by US-dollar cashier's check) and submit official English secondary transcripts (credential evaluation by IEE, WES or another NACES member is strongly encouraged and required for Cameroon, Gambia, Ghana, Haiti, Kenya, Liberia, Nigeria and Togo), a passport copy, proof of English (unless waived) and proof of funding for at least the first year before an immigration document is issued (bank statements or sponsor letter no more than six months old). No essay or recommendation is listed. The domestic application has no fee and needs no SAT/ACT. The Common Data Set rates GPA as very important and rigor as important.

deadlines.label: International fall admission deadline (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: The international page lists 'Fall Semester: July 1' without a year, so July 1, 2027 is assumed. International students already in the US with valid immigration status may apply until mid-August. IUP's Common Data Set shows an application closing date of 8/10 and rolling decisions beginning Sep 1 for the prior cycle; nothing is published about a priority date.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Residents of some countries are exempt (a separate IUP list). Also waived with a C or higher in a US college English composition course equivalent to ENGL 101 plus 12 college credits, or after completing nine credits of the American Language Institute (ALI) Bridge program. Students who attended a US high school may submit SAT/ACT or English AP scores, and TOEFL/IELTS can be requested at the Admissions Committee's discretion. IUP offers conditional (provisional) admission through the ALI intensive English program for students who meet every requirement except English.

english.notes: IUP TOEFL code 2652. Also accepted: TOEFL Essentials 4, TOEFL ITP 500 (through the ALI), GTEC CBT 1100. The page does not give a minimum on the new 1-6 TOEFL scale.

cost.notes: IUP billing page for 2026-27: tuition $8,338 (PA resident) and $12,090 (out-of-state) per year; international tuition is $10,348 per semester at 12-18 credits ($20,696 a year) and fees $2,706.60 per semester at 15 credits ($5,413 a year). Room $7,300 plus meal plan $4,708 (two-person semi-suite, 19 meals) = $12,008. Evacuation and repatriation fee $50 fall + $67 spring. Books $1,100 and other costs $2,080 (transportation $500 + $1,580) come from the Common Data Set. The total cost of attendance is the sum of these items ($41,414), before any Partial Tuition Waiver of up to $5,000 a year

aid.notes: International students are not eligible for federal aid. All degree-seeking F-1/J-1 students are reviewed automatically (no extra application) for a Partial Tuition Waiver: $2,500 per semester for full-time undergraduates ($210 per credit part-time), tied to 40 (20 part-time) hours of community service a semester; the page says recipients are chosen based on financial need, while the Common Data Set ticks non-need-based aid, so treat it as not guaranteed. Cook Honors College and athlete awards are different and cannot be combined. No international merit scholarship amounts are published.

sat.note: The international page gives no SAT code (SAT/ACT are optional).

act.note: The international page gives no ACT code.
